next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Important Election Dates

glance_notes.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Important Election Dates
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The voter registration deadline for Kansas's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 13, 2026. This is also the deadline to update a voter registration for a name or address change in order to participate in the General Election.

glance_notes.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Advance Voting Information
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Advance Voting: Any registered Kansas voter may vote in advance without providing an excuse. Advance voting is available by mail and in person. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, advance ballots may begin being mailed and in-person advance voting may begin October 14.

glance_notes.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Photo ID
glance_notes.text: Photo ID Required for In-Person Voting: Kansas generally requires voters to show an acceptable photo ID when voting in person, including during in-person advance voting. State law provides specific exemptions, including for certain permanent advance voters, qualifying military and overseas voters, and voters with qualifying religious objections.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Kansas residents may register online or by submitting a paper voter registration application. To register and vote, you must be a U.S. citizen, be a Kansas resident, be at least 18 years old by Election Day, and have completed the terms of any sentence resulting from a felony conviction. Online registration requires a valid Kansas driver's license or Kansas non-driver identification card. A person without one of those Kansas identification documents may register using a paper application. Voters must submit a new registration when changing their name, address or party affiliation.
register.glance_value: Register online or with a paper application
register.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Voter Registration
register.internal_note: The current Secretary of State voter registration page directly establishes citizenship, Kansas residence, age and felony-sentence eligibility requirements and confirms online and paper registration. The current voter information page at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/voter-information.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/voter-information.html) establishes that online registration requires a valid Kansas driver's license or non-driver identification card. The current registration form at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/forms/elections/voterregistration.pdf](https://www.sos.ks.gov/forms/elections/voterregistration.pdf) states that a person convicted of a felony must have received final discharge from imprisonment, parole or conditional release.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Kansas VoterView, available through the Kansas Secretary of State's official voter website, to check your voter registration information. VoterView also provides your polling location, sample ballot, advance mail ballot tracking information and voting history. Contact your county election office if your registration information needs to be updated or corrected.
check_registration.internal_note: The Secretary of State's July 27, 2026 voter-information announcement confirms that VoteKansas.gov is the official elections website and that its VoterView service provides polling location, sample ballot, advance mail ballot tracker and voting history. Supporting official source: [https://www.sos.ks.gov/media/press-releases/2026/07-27-26-election-website-for-kansas-voters.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/media/press-releases/2026/07-27-26-election-website-for-kansas-voters.html).

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Kansas voter registration closes 21 days before an election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline to register or update your voter registration for a name or address change is October 13, 2026. Registrations received after the deadline are not processed until after the election. Kansas does not provide general Election Day voter registration.
deadlines.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Important Election Dates
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 election calendar directly establishes October 13 as the General Election registration and name/address update deadline. The current voter registration page at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/voter-registration.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/voter-registration.html) establishes the 21-day registration-book closing rule and states that registrations received during the closed period are not processed until after the election.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Kansas voters can use the official VoterView service through VoteKansas.gov to find their Election Day polling location. Because a change of address can affect a voter's polling place, voters who have moved should update their registration by the applicable deadline and verify their location before Election Day. County election offices can also provide polling-place information.
polling_place.internal_note: The Secretary of State identifies VoterView as the official source for polling locations. The July 14, 2026 registration announcement at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/media/press-releases/2026/07-14-26-voter-registration-period-closes-today.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/media/press-releases/2026/07-14-26-voter-registration-period-closes-today.html) specifically warns that an address change may affect the polling location.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Kansas's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. State law generally requires polling places to be open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., but counties may establish different opening and closing times within limits set by law. Polling places must remain open for at least 12 consecutive hours, may open as early as 6:00 a.m. and may close as late as 8:00 p.m. Voters should verify their county's hours and polling location before voting. Voters casting a ballot in person generally must present acceptable photo identification. Anyone already in line when the polling location closes is allowed to vote.
election_day.glance_value: Verify local hours; polls open at least 12 hours
election_day.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Voter Information
election_day.internal_note: This is an important Kansas-specific distinction. The Secretary of State states that the statutory default is 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m., but counties may open as early as 6:00 a.m. and close as late as 8:00 p.m., provided polling locations remain open for at least 12 consecutive hours under K.S.A. 25-106. The official FAQ at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-faq.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-faq.html) confirms that voters in line when polls close may vote.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Kansas law sets 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. as the standard Election Day polling hours, but counties may adjust those hours. A county may open polling locations as early as 6:00 a.m. and close them as late as 8:00 p.m., and polling locations must be open for at least 12 consecutive hours. Check with your county election officer for the exact hours that apply to your polling place. Voters who are in line when the polls close are allowed to vote.
polling_hours.glance_value: Usually 7 a.m. – 7 p.m.; verify county hours
polling_hours.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Voter Information
polling_hours.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly states the 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. statutory hours, county authority to open as early as 6:00 a.m. and close as late as 8:00 p.m., and the requirement for at least 12 consecutive hours. The in-line-at-closing protection is confirmed by the official election FAQ at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-faq.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-faq.html).

early_voting.label: Advance In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Kansas allows registered voters to vote in person before Election Day without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, in-person advance voting may begin October 14. Every county must begin offering in-person advance voting no later than October 27. Advance voting is conducted at county election offices and, where offered, satellite locations. Exact starting dates, locations and hours vary by county, so voters should check the official county-specific information before going to vote.
early_voting.glance_value: May begin October 14; all counties by October 27
early_voting.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Important Election Dates
early_voting.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar directly establishes October 14 as the first possible day for advance voting and October 27 as the date by which in-person advance voting must begin in all counties. The Secretary of State advance-voting page at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/advance-voting-information.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/advance-voting-information.html) confirms that advance voting may occur at county election offices and satellite locations. County schedules are published at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/advance-voting-locations.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/advance-voting-locations.html) and should be rechecked when General Election schedules are finalized.

absentee_mail.label: Advance Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Kansas voter may request an advance ballot by mail without providing an excuse. A voter must submit an advance-ballot application and provide a driver's license number or a copy of acceptable photo identification as required by state law. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, advance ballots may begin being transmitted on October 14. Voters should return completed ballots as early as possible. Kansas law states that ballots are due by the close of polls on Election Day, but a current statewide court injunction requires election officials to count qualifying ballots postmarked by Election Day if they arrive by the last postal delivery on the Friday after the election. Because that litigation may change the applicable rule, voters should not rely on the extended arrival period and should ensure their ballot reaches election officials by the close of polls on Election Day whenever possible.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; return by Election Day when possible
absentee_mail.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Advance Voting Information
absentee_mail.flagged_reason: Kansas's statutory mail-ballot receipt deadline is currently affected by an active statewide court injunction. The Secretary of State states that the injunction requires ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted if received by the last postal delivery on the Friday after the election, while advising voters to return ballots by the close of polls on Election Day.
absentee_mail.internal_note: This section requires close monitoring before the General Election. The Secretary of State's current official page expressly explains the conflict between the statutory Election Day receipt deadline and the statewide Douglas County District Court injunction, and states that the Kansas Court of Appeals rejected the Secretary's request to stay the injunction. Do not state an unconditional Election Day receipt deadline while the injunction remains operative. The official FAQ at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-faq.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-faq.html) confirms that no excuse is required for advance voting by mail and that voters generally apply for each election.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Kansas generally requires voters to show photo identification when voting in person, including during in-person advance voting. Accepted identification includes a driver's license or identification card issued by Kansas or another U.S. state or district, U.S. passport, U.S. military identification, identification issued by a Native American tribe, government employee identification, student identification from an accredited Kansas postsecondary institution, a concealed-carry license issued by Kansas or another state or district, or a public-assistance identification card issued by a government office. If an identification document has an expiration date, it generally must not be expired. Voters age 65 or older may use an expired photo ID. Other exemptions exist for certain permanent advance voters, military and overseas voters and their spouses and dependents, and voters with qualifying religious objections.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID generally required for in-person voting
voter_id.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Photo ID
voter_id.internal_note: The current Secretary of State photo-ID page directly lists the eight accepted categories and current exemptions. A registered voter who lacks approved government-issued photo identification may apply for a free Kansas nondriver ID. Kansas also provides a process for qualifying voters who lack underlying identity documents to obtain a free Kansas birth certificate or, for certain people born outside Kansas, a State Voter Identification Document.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Kansas provides voting assistance and accessible voting options for voters with disabilities. Polling places must provide accessible voting equipment, and voters who need assistance have the right to receive help with voting subject to applicable law. A voter with a permanent illness or disability may apply for permanent advance voting status so that an advance ballot is automatically sent for eligible elections. Voters should contact their county election office for specific accessibility arrangements, accessible equipment and assistance available at their voting location.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible voting and permanent advance status available
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State voter resources specifically provide accessibility guidance for voters with disabilities and voters needing assistance. The state's accessibility guidance establishes accessible voting booths and ballots and voter assistance rights. The current election statistics page at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-statistics.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-statistics.html) confirms that voters with a permanent illness or disability may request permanent advance-by-mail status through their county election office.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Kansas provides special voting procedures for eligible active-duty military members, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living abroad under the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act. Eligible voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to request a ballot through the county election office associated with their Kansas residence. Kansas does not require a qualifying UOCAVA voter to already be registered in the county in order to vote under these procedures. A voter who files a Federal Post Card Application before the primary will automatically receive a ballot for the General Election that year. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Kansas must transmit requested UOCAVA ballots by September 19.
military_overseas.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Citizens
military_overseas.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly establishes UOCAVA coverage, FPCA use, the rule that qualifying voters need not already be registered in the county, and automatic General Election ballot receipt after an FPCA filed before the primary. The official 2026 election calendar at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/important-election-dates.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/important-election-dates.html) establishes September 19 as the General Election UOCAVA transmission deadline. The state page notes that there is no statutory FPCA application deadline but applications must be submitted early enough to allow ballot transmission and return.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register and vote in Kansas if they are U.S. citizens, Kansas residents and otherwise meet the state's voter qualifications. A student who establishes a Kansas residence may register using that residence, while a student who remains a resident of another state should follow that state's voting rules. Kansas does not impose a minimum duration of state residence beyond meeting the applicable voter registration deadline. For in-person voting, a student identification card issued by an accredited postsecondary educational institution in Kansas is an accepted form of photo identification.
student_voting.glance_value: Kansas-resident students may register and use qualifying student ID
student_voting.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Photo ID
student_voting.internal_note: The current Secretary of State photo-ID page directly establishes that student ID from an accredited Kansas postsecondary institution is accepted for in-person voting. Kansas Election Standards Chapter I, [https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-standards/Kansas-Election-Standards-Chapter-I-Voter-Registration.pdf](https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-standards/Kansas-Election-Standards-Chapter-I-Voter-Registration.pdf), states that the constitutional qualifications are age, citizenship and Kansas residence and that there is no separate length-of-residency requirement beyond timely registration. The reader-facing section intentionally does not claim that merely attending a Kansas college automatically establishes Kansas residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Kansas voters can view their sample ballot through the official VoterView service beginning 45 days before an election. Sample ballots may also be requested from the local election office or viewed at the polling place. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's address and districts, use VoterView to obtain the ballot information that applies to your registration.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Available in VoterView 45 days before the election
sample_ballot.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — VoteKansas.gov / VoterView
sample_ballot.internal_note: The current Secretary of State election FAQ at [https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-faq.html](https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/election-faq.html) directly states that sample ballots can be viewed online starting 45 days before an election or requested from the local election office or polling place. The Secretary's July 27, 2026 announcement confirms that VoterView through VoteKansas.gov provides sample ballots.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Kansas Secretary of State, Docking State Office Building, 915 SW Harrison Street, Topeka, KS 66612. Main phone: 785-296-4564. Elections Division voter hotline: 800-262-VOTE (8683). Elections Division email: election@ks.gov. General Secretary of State email: kssos@ks.gov. Office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. For questions about an individual voter registration, polling place, advance ballot or local advance-voting schedule, contact your county election office.
contact.source_name: Kansas Secretary of State — Elections Division
contact.internal_note: Current Secretary of State pages directly verify the Docking State Office Building address, 785-296-4564 main phone, 800-262-VOTE Elections Division number, [election@ks.gov](mailto:election@ks.gov) Elections Division email, [kssos@ks.gov](mailto:kssos@ks.gov) general email and 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. office hours. Email addresses are intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto syntax.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use VoteKansas.gov and the Kansas Secretary of State Elections website for official statewide voter information. VoterView provides polling locations, sample ballots, advance mail ballot tracking and voting history. County election officers administer voter registration, polling places, advance voting locations and advance ballots locally. Voters should use official Kansas government election resources and their county election office for election-specific information.
